prompt_edits: ENFORCE UNIQUE FINDING IDs AND PRE-MERGE DEDUPLICATION: The current register contains severe ID collisions — CH18-01 appears 4 times for different issues, CH19-01 appears 4 times, CH15-01 appears 3 times, and at least 15 other IDs are reused. Additionally, cross-model duplicates exist under different IDs (CH16-002 ≡ CH16-02; CH9-FIG92-RING-INDEX ≡ FIG-9.2-01; CH2-OCC-01 two instances). Edit: 'Assign each finding a globally unique ID using {chapter/figure/table}-{section}-{sequence}. Never reuse an ID for a different issue. Before merging registers from multiple models, run a deduplication pass: if two findings reference the same location and describe the same underlying problem, merge them under one ID and list all contributing models. Report the deduplication count in the merged register.'

ADD A MANDATORY CROSS-CHAPTER CANONICAL-VALUE LEDGER PASS: Several models independently found cross-chapter consistency issues (TTFT across Ch 2/4, SLO targets across Ch 6/14/15, prefix-reuse assumptions across Ch 17/19, candidate evaluations across Ch 12/13, unit basis across Ch 7 sections), but these were found inconsistently — some models caught them, others missed them entirely. Edit: 'Before the final register is compiled, extract every reused canonical value (SLO targets, host counts, memory budgets, cost figures, model specifications, concurrency limits, prefix-reuse rates, occupancy thresholds) into a single ledger table with ALL locations where each value appears. Flag any value that differs across locations without an explicit assumption change as ONE root-cause issue with all dependent anchors. This pass is mandatory and must be performed even if no cross-chapter issues were found during the main review.'

REQUIRE SPECIFIC, CHECKABLE SEMANTIC CLAIMS FOR FIGURE FINDINGS: Many figure findings are unique to a single model (FIG-8.1-01, FIG-10.1-01/02/03, FIG-11.2-01, FIG-11.3-01, FIG-15.1-01, FIG-17.1-01, FIG-A5-01, etc.), suggesting inconsistent application of the figure semantic audit. Edit: 'For each figure finding, the reviewer must state a SPECIFIC, CHECKABLE semantic claim in the form: [caption/label/annotation X says/shows A] but [figure content/prose/arithmetic shows/implies B]. A figure finding that cannot be stated as a specific, falsifiable mismatch between two observable elements should be marked NEEDS-VERIFICATION rather than filed as a defect. This forces the reviewer to identify the exact semantic error rather than filing a general concern about the figure.'

Add a mandatory canonical-value ledger keyed by exact scenario/quantity (e.g., 8.6 s service, 436 GB pool, 6.24M req/mo, 21 hosts) with chapter/page anchors. Require every P0/P1 numeric finding to cite the ledger entry and include the full quoted clause with its operator. This prevents duplicate IDs and makes cross-chapter contradictions one root cause.

Require a structured figure-semantic signoff for every figure: page, figure number, caption, drawn labels/arrows/quantities, and a check against prose/arithmetic. Explicitly flag duplicate figures and reject 'figure missing' findings from text chunks. The current register shows many figure findings from only one model, indicating uneven vision coverage.

Require event-trace reconstruction and conservation/budget closure for every multi-call, cache, fallback, burst-buffer, or cost example: build the per-call table (input, output, prefill, cache reuse, tool wait, success class) and verify components sum to the total before judging summary formulas. This would catch the Ch16/18/19/23/24/26 cost and cache contradictions more uniformly.

Require every register entry to carry a stable UUID and the full untruncated quoted clause, including the exact operator and enough surrounding context to reproduce the claim; the current 300-character truncation makes independent adjudication impossible for many entries.

Require a per-finding verification ledger containing artifact hash, PDF page, printed page, source span, recomputation or rendered-page evidence, and an explicit NOT VERIFIED marker when the reviewer did not actually inspect the source; cross-critique must not adjudicate from summary text alone.

Require any refile of a round-1 rejected class to cite the new primary evidence that distinguishes it from the previously confirmed benign reading; otherwise the entry should be automatically marked as a false positive.

Make the canonical-value ledger a mandatory, separately emitted deliverable rather than an instruction buried in the finding mechanisms. Require one row per reused canonical quantity (70B weights at 140 GB FP16 / 70 GB 8-bit; KV 2.621 MB/token FP16 and 1.311 MB/token 8-bit at the canonical full-MHA reference; 640 GB host pool; 436 GB KV budget = 640 - 140 - 64; 9,200-token canonical request; 8.6 s service time; 6.24M req/mo; 21 hosts; C ~ 17.5; ~2.0 rps; TTFT 1.2 s / TPOT 50 ms; H100 989 TFLOPS and 3.35 TB/s), with EVERY anchor page and the value at each anchor, and require the model to flag any row whose anchors disagree. Rationale: this round produced roughly 140 local findings but no ledger-level root cause, even though the prompt names this ledger in §2.2 - it was treated as a suggestion and skipped. Also require the ledger to record the operator used at each anchor (=, ~, <=, 'up to') so that the next round's false-positive pass can apply the approximation rule mechanically instead of re-deriving it per finding.

Require a per-chapter coverage matrix and an explicit 'reviewed and clean' declaration for every chapter, and extend the mandatory review targets to the front matter, the glossary, the reference list, and the index. Rationale: the merged register contains zero findings for the preface/roadmap, the glossary, the bibliography, and the index, and only one or two for Ch 1, Ch 11, Ch 14, Ch 20, Ch 21, and Ch 22 - in a 458-page book that pattern is far more likely to mean 'not reviewed' than 'nothing wrong'. Silence must be distinguishable from a clean pass. Add a required reference-audit deliverable: for each citation, the primary-source status, the date, and whether the cited work actually supports the adjacent claim, with a specific list of claims that carry no source.

Fix the register schema so that findings arrive adjudicable: (a) do not truncate the issue records - the 300-character cap destroyed root_cause, correction, and acceptance_test, which the schema itself requires, so roughly 140 entries arrived non-actionable and could not be adjudicated on content; emit a compact index (id, severity, page, one-line claim) plus full records stored per model instead. (b) Require globally unique IDs with a namespace, and run a dedup/merge step before cross-critique: this round reused at least fourteen IDs for materially different issues (CH15-02, CH16-01, CH16-02, CH18-01 through CH18-04, CH19-01, CH23-02, CH23-03, CH23-04, CH24-01, CH25-01, CH25-04, CH26-01, CH26-02, FIG-1.1-01) and filed at least eight issues twice under different IDs (CH2-01/CH2-OCC-01, CH16-002/CH16-02, CH9-FIG92-RING-INDEX/FIG-9.2-01, FIG-6.1-1/FIG-6.1-01, FIG-6.2-1/FIG-6.2-01, FIG-15.1-1/FIG-15.1-01, EQ-352-01/EQ-332-01, APPA-01 twice); the outer 'id' field was null for every entry, so any automated merge keyed on it would have silently failed. (c) Unify the severity vocabulary (the register mixes P0-P3 with CRITICAL/MAJOR/MODERATE/MINOR) and require every P1 to name the specific wrong architecture decision it would cause, with a stated cap on the P1 population - roughly 100 P1s out of 140 findings is not a usable priority signal.
